target.title: fix(dashboard): keep OpenClaw Bay terminal outcomes visible
target.body:
## Summary

- keep distinct, proved OpenClaw Bay terminal outcomes visible instead of silently rendering only the first six
- use up to 12 staggered terminal slots per pool; choose three columns only when the rendered terminal shoreline is at least 320px wide, otherwise retain a readable two-column layout
- make lane conversations vary naturally while keeping them explicitly non-operational flavour text

## Problem

The public Bay counter correctly reflected the shared tide buffer, but the visual pool used a fixed six-item slice. For example, a `9 / 20` counter could show only six completed crustaceans with no indication that three were hidden.

## Implementation

- expand terminal-pool capacity from six to 12 items and add staggered 12-slot layouts for both two- and three-column pools
- grow the completed pool within the available shoreline; after 12 items, show an explicit `+N more in the tide buffer` note instead of silently hiding records
- select three columns from the actual `#terminal-stack` width, not a viewport guess; a 320px threshold preserves readable reference labels on constrained widths and reflows on resize
- add deterministic variations for chat questions and replies, retaining the elapsed value when available without claiming queue progress
- force the Linux proof runner to retain LF line endings on Windows checkouts

## API and performance boundary

This is presentation and proof work only. It does not change the Worker status schema, terminal-buffer merge/tide logic, dashboard cache, or browser polling cadence. Bay remains a cache-backed `/api/status` reader at 20 seconds (three browser-to-Worker requests per minute, compared with Overview's 15-second cadence), and the browser proof records zero direct GitHub API and zero mutation requests. Upstream GitHub refreshes remain cache-dependent.

## Validation and proof

- `pnpm run build:dashboard`
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `node --test --test-name-pattern "OpenClaw Bay is an unlisted" test/dashboard-worker.test.ts`
- `node --check docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- deterministic Chromium proof via Crabbox `local-container`, lease `cbx_320bf6be31c9` (`blue-lobster`), image `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble`
  - exact source: `2d5793c1a0e1b39fd174c3d743118845152eaab6`
  - 25 assertions and 17 evidence frames passed
  - proves nine completed outcomes render individually, the constrained-width two-column layout has zero reference-label intersections, and the wide layout returns to three columns
  - zero direct GitHub API requests, mutation requests, console errors, and uncaught page errors

Tracked evidence:

- [`proof-summary.json`](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/proof-summary.json)
- [`playwright-proof-storyboard.jpg`](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/playwright-proof-storyboard.jpg)
- [`trace.zip`](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/trace.zip)

Codex review closeout:

- `codex review --uncommitted`: clean after the accepted responsive-layout and proof-refresh findings were fixed
- `codex review --base origin/main`: clean; no actionable defects after the final retry (the first attempt timed out while inspecting the binary proof package)

## Risks and rollout

The only user-facing change is the Bay demo's terminal-pool layout and ambient chat copy. The tide counter and terminal-state semantics are unchanged. This follows the original experiment in #499 and needs no new configuration, credentials, or deployment path.
